items.summary: EMA’s Head of the Stakeholders…, A new Head of the Veterinary…, Ivo Claassen joined EMA in 2018. Among many career highlights, Ivo and his team worked with the veterinary medicines network on the successful implementation of the 2019…

items.title: Merck, Moderna’s personalized cancer vaccine slows recurrence in phase 3, setting up approval push
items.summary: Merck & Co. and Moderna's personalized mRNA cancer vaccine has successfully lengthened recurrence-free survival when paired with Keytruda for patients with high-risk skin cancer. The phase 3 win sets the partners up to potentially seek accelerated approval.

items.title: Amylyx readies approval push after GLP-1 inhibitor halves blood sugar crashes in ph. 3 win
items.summary: Amylyx Pharmaceuticals’ $35 million bet on the GLP-1 receptor antagonist avexitide appears to have paid off, with the molecule cutting the number of dangerous blood sugar crashes by more than half in patients with a rare endocrine disease.

items.title: Regulatory tracker: J&J scores EU approval for Tecvayli-Darzalex combo
items.summary: In this tracker, Fierce Pharma is recording the regulatory progress of in-market products, including expansions into key geographies and new indications. Some of these updates may not meet the bar for standalone stories, but we think they are still worth mentioning.

items.title: Xspray's Dasynoc approval bid foiled again by FDA's manufacturer concerns
items.summary: Less than a year after the FDA turned down the resubmitted application for the company’s leukemia prospect Dasynoc, Xspray Pharma has again hit a wall at the U.S. regulator.

items.title: Lilly’s long-acting insulin wins NICE blessing ahead of potential UK approval
items.summary: Hundreds of thousands of patients with type 2 diabetes could eventually make the switch to a weekly insulin injection and reduce their annual injections by 85% after NICE, the U.K.’s drug cost watchdog, gave Lilly's Onswik its seal of approval for NHS coverage.

items.title: Regeneron's Pasatru scores FDA approval in ultra-rare bone lesions disorder
items.summary: Regeneron's Pasatru has crossed the finish line with FDA approval after more than ten years of development. The drug is only the second approved treatment for FOP, an ultra-rare genetic condition that causes patients' soft tissues to turn to bone.

items.title: SK strikes settlement with MSN over future Xcopri generic: reports
items.summary: For the first time, SK Biopharmaceuticals has reached a settlement with a generics manufacturer that has applied for FDA approval of a copycat version of its epilepsy treatment Xcopri, local news outlets report. SK’s deal with India’s MSN Laboratories will allow the Korean company to extend its market exclusivity beyond October 2032, when the protection for

items.title: Aurobindo unit, China API maker dinged in latest round of FDA warning letters
items.summary: After receiving a checkered regulatory scorecard in 2024, Aurobindo’s sterile injectables and oncology unit is back in the FDA’s crosshairs.

items.title: Werewolf transforms into Ambros via reverse merger to support phase 3 push for rare disease drug
items.summary: Werewolf Therapeutics’ hunt for strategic alternatives has ended. Ambros Therapeutics has agreed to merge with Werewolf in an all-stock deal and has raised $150 million, positioning the biotech to take its lead rare disease drug candidate through to a filing for approval.

items.title: Meet Aletta: The first FDA approved robotic blood draw device
items.summary: The FDA has approved Vitestro’s Aletta as the first standalone robotic device in the U.S. designed to draw blood without the need for hands-on human help.

items.title: Merck-Moderna cancer vaccine win spurs stock jump, speculation of Keytruda-like impact
items.summary: As the dust settles on phase 3 data that added $45 billion to Moderna’s market cap, analysts have begun to ask a question that could define cancer care in the coming years: Can use of the vaccine be as broad as Keytruda?

items.title: ‘Money has spoken’: Why Chinese biotech CEOs tell Fierce they’re unfazed about rising US tensions
items.summary: You might assume Chinese biotechs are enduring sleepless nights worrying about whether the ramping up of rhetoric in the U.S. is putting their new financial gains in peril. But the companies Fierce spoke to remained unconcerned.

items.title: Amgen abandoning $500M+ Crohn’s collab won’t derail TScan’s pipeline strategy
items.summary: TScan has told Fierce that its pipeline strategy remains unchanged despite Amgen walking away from a Crohn’s disease collaboration that had the potential for a windfall of half a billion dollars.

items.title: Trump taps White House aide Heidi Overton as nominee for next FDA commissioner
items.summary: After three months without a permanent leader in place, President Donald Trump has named his pick for the new commissioner of the FDA. Heidi Overton, M.D., Ph.D., currently a White House aide, will go before the Senate in an effort to secure the job of the country’s top drug regulator.

items.title: Kolon TissueGene shrinks workforce after pivotal osteoarthritis trial miss
items.summary: Following a phase 3 knee osteoarthritis failure that its CEO acknowledged caused “great disappointment and concern,” Kolon TissueGene is laying off 37 employees at its Maryland headquarters.

items.title: Fierce Pharma Asia—China's IIT scrutiny; Daiichi Sankyo, AZ ph. 3 win; Leo, Tanabe's dermatology deal
items.summary: China's investigator-initiated trials, once praised for their speediness, have been drawn into scrutiny for a lack of transparency. AstraZeneca and Daiichi Sankyo's Enhertu earned a win in a phase 3 non-small cell lung cancer trial. Tanabe Pharma secured a $435 million payout for global rights to its dermatology rare disease treatment dersimelagon.

items.title: Pursuing patient options, Novo kicks off trial testing smaller doses of Wegovy pill
items.summary: Just eight months after it introduced its Wegovy pill, Novo Nordisk is testing the GLP-1 in smaller doses in the phase 3 OASIS 5 study.

items.title: Ultragenyx, after FDA speed bump, lands 1st gene therapy nod with green light in glycogen storage disease
items.summary: If at first you don’t succeed in gene therapy, then try, try again, is the lesson Ultragenyx likely took home this week, pocketing its first FDA nod in the class a little over a year after a separate program stalled on manufacturing grounds.

items.title: Biokin bispecific ADC iza-bren hits goal in lung cancer trial, boosting case for BMS’ global test
items.summary: Biokin Pharma’s iza-bren, a first-in-class antibody-drug conjugate partnered with Bristol Myers Squibb, has posted another positive phase 3 readout.

items.title: How Pharma Teams Evaluate Biotech Companies for Partnerships and Acquisitions
items.summary: Addressing how interactions around partnerships or acquisitions differ from those of investment from biotech companies and how CMOs can support those conversations.

items.title: Boehringer places phase 1 study of investigational drug on hold to examine ‘safety event’
items.summary: Boehringer Ingelheim has suspended a phase 1 trial of an investigational small molecule drug while it seeks to understand a “safety event,” although the German pharma isn't shedding light on the nature of the incident for now.

items.title: Boehringer Ingelheim again rises up rare disease reputation rankings
items.summary: Boehringer Ingelheim has continued its rise up patient groups’ ranking of rare disease companies, adding to last year’s gains to cement its status toward the top of the leaderboards. But the German drugmaker failed to crack the top three of the full table, which the same three companies occupied again.

items.title: Chutes & Ladders—Neumora shuffles leadership ahead of IND
items.summary: Joshua Pinto, Ph.D., has been appointed chief executive officer of Neumora Therapeutics, a clinical-stage biotech with obesity and neuro assets.

items.title: Why Pheast’s CEO has no regrets about transparent approach to R&D despite competitors circling
items.summary: Pheast Therapeutics may have learned the hard way about the risks of competitors getting a glimpse of your heard-earned discoveries, but the immuno-oncology startup is so far sticking to its transparent approach.

items.title: Chai tees up Bristol Myers Squibb AI antibody discovery collab
items.summary: A month after Chai Discovery tied up a major $400 million series C funding round, the AI drug discovery firm has teamed up with Bristol Myers Squibb.

items.title: Lilly pens deal with Gateway Labs resident Amplitude for RNA vaccine platform for infectious disease
items.summary: Eli Lilly has turned to one of its Gateway Labs residents to help the Big Pharma develop trans-amplifying RNA (taRNA) vaccines for infectious diseases.

items.title: A ‘renaissance for biomedicine’: human brain organoids model development for 5 years
items.summary: Scientists’ ability to recapitulate the human brain in a dish has always been hindered by the inability to model the full capacity of the brain and its development through time.

items.title: Tolerance Bio jumps into phase 2 with $260M deal for thymus-targeting fusion protein
items.summary: Tolerance Bio has vaulted into the clinic by agreeing to pay NeoImmuneTech up to $260 million for rights to a fusion protein in certain thymus-related indications in the Americas and Europe.

items.title: New Biotech-Academia Partnership Approaches to Empower the Drug Development Ecosystem
items.summary: Addressing shifts in the global clinical development ecosystem and how academia and biotech can better partner to develop new therapies for patients.

items.title: Developing a Global Clinical Trial Strategy for Emerging Biotechs
items.summary: Discussing how small biotechs can accelerate clinical development with fit-for-purpose global clinical trial strategies.

items.title: Merck and Sarah Cannon team up to boost oncology trial efficiency
items.summary: Oncology R&D organization Sarah Cannon Research Institute (SCRI) announced a collaboration with Merck & Co. to increase patient access to oncology trials at community-based sites in the U.S.

items.title: Craif raises $33M to boost work on its urine test for cancer
items.summary: The AI biopharma Craif has raised $33 million in its series D funding round as it also adds a new exec, bringing its total capital raised to date to $88 million.

items.title: Johnson & Johnson MedTech nabs Monarch Quest 3 update for lung cancer detection
items.summary: Johnson & Johnson MedTech has been handed its fourth major software launch in the past 18 months for its Monarch bronchoscopy robot.

items.title: Fierce Biotech Layoff Tracker 2026: Kolon cuts workforce after ph. 3 fail; Sanofi sheds 229 staffers
items.summary: As always, if you know of layoffs occurring at a biotech, please reach out to the Fierce Biotech editorial team.

items.title: BioMarin bulks up bone unit with $275M Alesta buyout to challenge AstraZeneca
items.summary: BioMarin Pharmaceutical has agreed to buy Alesta Therapeutics for $275 million upfront, positioning the biopharma to challenge AstraZeneca in the rare bone disease market.

items.title: Fierce Biotech Fundraising Tracker '26: Abcuro secures $66M; InduPro assembles $77M
items.summary: The Fierce Biotech Fundraising Tracker records venture capital rounds of $50 million or more secured by biotechs.

items.title: Lundbeck continues neuroscience evolution as CEO keeps company ‘punching above its weight’
items.summary: Almost three years into his tenure as Lundbeck’s CEO, Charl van Zyl is confident the company can prove its mettle as a “neuroscience challenger” capable of “punching above its weight.”

items.title: The Oral GLP-1 Tracker: Novo's Wegovy pill back on track as Lilly's momentum slows
items.summary: Fierce Pharma is launching the weekly Oral GLP-1 Tracker, leveraging analysts’ notes and IQVIA data to monitor prescription trends and shifting market shares as Novo Nordisk's Wegovy pill and Eli Lilly's Foundayo vie to become the go-to oral weight-loss solution for millions.
